vectors.name: parse-unclosed-list
vectors.note: PARSE rejects the configuration rather than one signal, so it is the one code that is not a per-signal failure

vectors.name: arity-if-missing-else
vectors.note: else is mandatory: an if with no else would have to invent a value for the missing branch

vectors.name: no-signal-attribute-without-context
vectors.note: evaluating a signal-dependent expression with SIGNAL_NONE is an error, never a null (ABI §7.1)

vectors.name: missing-attribute-present-signal
vectors.note: missing data is an error, not null — the invariant that keeps a config typo from becoming a 2 a.m. mystery

vectors.name: type-function-as-final-result
vectors.note: A function cannot be an expression's result: there is no CBOR value for one, so the property would have nothing to hand the guest.

vectors.name: type-applying-a-non-function
vectors.note: A list head, so the fault is only findable at evaluation and TYPE is normative. A literal or sigil head is rejected statically instead (10).

vectors.name: domain-int-overflow
vectors.note: Ints are i64 (§2); overflow is an error rather than a wrap, because a silently wrapped threshold is a control decision made on a wrong number.
